steps.title: Start with the application story
steps.summary: HAL begins with a readable explanation of identity, activity, source, and confidence—not a wall of collector output.
steps.takeaway: You should understand the main story without opening a map.

steps.title: Separate observation from inference
steps.summary: A running process is an observed instance. Its connection to an application includes direction, confidence, and supporting evidence.
steps.takeaway: HAL shows why a connection exists instead of presenting it as magic.

steps.title: Explain why software may return
steps.summary: Startup declarations appear separately from current processes. Their presence does not prove that the application is running now.
steps.takeaway: Current activity and persistence are different questions.

steps.title: Distinguish support data from rebuildable data
steps.summary: Application support can contain valuable user state. Rebuildable caches are described separately, with ownership evidence and no deletion action.
steps.takeaway: Observed location is not permission to remove it.

steps.title: Use maps for supporting context
steps.summary: The Relationship Map explains connections. The Filesystem Map explains location. Both support the application story instead of replacing it.
steps.takeaway: Open the maps when you want to investigate the evidence.
